jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**As BMS Supporter (Adv. Utilities Professional), you will plan and deliver the facility and utility projects that keep our aseptic filling factory in Bagsværd moving forward. You will drive changes to BMS/FMS, from automation and control systems to alarm set-up, and see them through to implementation. With major equipment optimisations ahead, you will help shape the future setup of your area and support the reliable production of insulin, GLP-1 and weight-reducing products for people around the world.

**What You’ll Bring

**You have a technical mindset, enjoy working with improvements and thrive where priorities shift. To be considered, you have:

• A relevant technical background, for example a degree in mechanical engineering or similar.

• Strong Danish and English skills, as we work in an international environment.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to interact with people at all levels of the organisation.

• A proactive, ambitious approach and the flexibility to work during the two annual production stops, which usually fall in July/August and December/January.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Experience with validation of systems.

• Experience with BMS/FMS.

• Experience in the pharmaceutical industry.

**What You’ll Do

**You will turn technical changes into safe, well-documented improvements in a production environment that cannot stand still. In practice, you will:

• Plan and execute projects with a focus on BMS/FMS changes, such as automation, control systems and alarm set-up.

• Prepare validation documentation for your projects.

• Communicate and coordinate with internal stakeholders and external contractors, so everyone knows what is happening and when.

• Supervise the implementation phase of projects during the factory production stops, twice a year.

• Contribute to equipment optimisations and changes in the coming years, helping shape the future setup of your area.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will be part of Drug Product Manufacturing at Site Bagsværd (DPM BA), an aseptic filling factory with approximately 900 employees producing marketed insulin, GLP-1 and weight-reducing products for the benefit of patients worldwide. Within Global Manufacturing & Supply, you will join the Facility/Utility Projects team, which maintains and delivers project implementation within WFI, clean steam, compressed air and ventilation (HVAC), as well as improvements and refurbishments of the production facility.

You will work closely with experienced colleagues, skilled workers and stakeholders across the organisation, as well as external contractors. Your manager will be Ehab El-sayed.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will work in an engaging environment where you can build your skills alongside experienced colleagues and see the result of your work on the factory floor. With equipment optimisations and changes ahead, you will have room to contribute your ideas, take ownership of your projects and grow with the area as it develops.

You will be supported to perform at your best, and trusted to speak up when things stall and to follow decisions through. The production stops call for increased flexibility, and the work rewards people who stay clear on priorities and act with urgency.

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200 DKK - 838,100 DKK (DK), corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn technical know-how into progress for people who rely on our products, apply for the BMS Supporter role by 11 November 2026.

For further information, please contact Ehab El-sayed, Senior Manager, at 30757584.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) has a leading position in research related to breeding for sustainability related traits in dairy cattle such as feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane emissions. This is enabled by an ambitious farm based infrastructure with large scale measurement of methane emissions, feed intake, feed and environment parameters, productivity, and novel phenotypes on individual cows, based on collaboration with industry and international researchers. The successful candidate for these positions will join our team to further advance in the areas of feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane. This includes phenotype definition, genotype by environment studies, variance component estimation, and integrating novel genetically related traits using digital tools or functional genomic information or OMICS to improve genomic prediction models. The successful candidate will collaborate with industry partners, support teaching at undergraduate and graduate levels, and co-supervise Master's, and PhD students. The candidate is expected to help with creating a collaborative work environment within and outside QGG that integrates novel innovative research programs towards the green transition in animal agriculture.

The position is a full-time position for a period of 2 years, starting on 1 March 2027. There are possibilities for extension to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and funding is available. If your research profile does not completely match the descriptions above but you have a theoretical background and are interested in developing one of the research areas mentioned, QGG would like to hear your motivation for seeking this position.

The position offers you:
• Contribute to ongoing projects in the area of feed- and nitrogen efficiency, resilience, and methane
• Advance the genetic modeling of these traits, including genotype by environment interactions, and OMICS
• Participate in project applications
• Collaborate with diverse group of researchers nationally and internationally
• Engage with commercial breeding organizations
• Publish high-quality research in peer-reviewed journals and at conferences
• Support in teaching, and (co-)supervise BSc, MSc and PhD students – though teaching duties may be low
 

The ideal candidate:
• Holds a PhD with a strong background in quantitative genetics and/or animal breeding
• Has published high-quality research in peer-reviewed journals
• Experience with one or more scripting language (e.g., R, Python, Julia) and/or genetic software (e.g., DMU, ASReml)
• Can biologically interpret results and relate to breeding decision making
• Exhibits excellent teamwork skills and has experience collaborating with scientists across different disciplines nationally and internationally
• Possesses effective communication skills and can communicate complex scientific concepts to diverse audiences, whether in academia, industry, or society.
• Shows interest in teaching and mentoring of BSc, MSc and PhD-students

Who we are:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a vibrant and exciting interdisciplinary center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). QGG is an international organization with more than 70 employees and visiting researchers from more than 20 countries. We perform basic and applied research within plant, livestock and human quantitative genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and precision medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. QGG is located at the central campus in Aarhus and at the AU Flakkebjerg campus in newly renovated offices with well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, equipment, and highperforming computing clusters.

Place of work: 
The place of work is C.F. Møllers Allé 3, Bldg. 1130, 8000 Aarhus C. The area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information:
For further information please contact Associate professor: Bingjie Li, email: bingjie.li@qgg.au.dk, telephone: +45 71879527, or Tenure Track Assistant Professor Rasmus Bak Stephansen, e-mail: rasmus.stephansen@qgg.au.dk, mobile: +45 61764959.

Application Deadline: 
29th November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

jobs.description:
Aarhus University - an international top 100 University - has made an ambitious strategic investment in expanding the Department of Computer Science. We expect to hire up to three candidates in 2027. Therefore, the department invites applications from candidates in computer science that are driven by excellence in research and teaching as well as a strong interest for innovation and addressing societal challenges.

The call is open rank, i.e. we are looking for tenure-track Assistant Professors, Associate Professors and Full Professors. The successful candidates will have a unique opportunity to shape the continued expansion of our computer science department.

The department consists of four Sections: Algorithms, Data and Artificial Intelligence (ADA); Cryptography and Cybersecurity (CRC); Human-Centered Computing (HCC); Programming Languages, Logic, and Software Security (PLS).

We are looking for applicants to strengthen and expand the above Sections, but topics beyond, or across sections are also welcome. We are, in particular, looking for applicants with competencies in the following topics:

• Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence
• Learning Theory
• Algorithms and Complexity
• NLP/Large Language Models,
• Generative Media Foundation Models
• Human-AI-Interaction
• Explainable and Trustworthy AI
• Data Management, Databases and Data Mining
• Economics and Computation
• Game Theory and Decision-Making
• Quantum Algorithms and Programming
• Software Engineering and Programming Languages
We generally encourage candidates within all areas of Computer Science – not restricted to the mentioned topics – to apply.

For full professorship candidates, we expect - in addition to excellent research and teaching in their field - that the candidates can demonstrate leadership, visions, collaborations and societal impact for the entire computer science department.

We provide starting packages with PhD funding (depending on position) and operational expenses for the first three years.

We wish to build a computer science research and study environment with equality and diversity as a core value for recruitment as well as for daily study and work life. If you have visions for or experience with activities or initiatives to support such core values in a computer science context, we encourage you to describe them in your application.

The starting date is flexible, from August 1st, 2027, and onwards.

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Åbogade 34, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Further information on the position can be obtained from Head of Department, Professor Kaj Grønbæk kgronbak@cs.au.dk.

About Department of Computer Science at Aarhus University

The Department of Computer Science is located in a developing campus area called IT-City Katrinebjerg, where many R&D institutions and companies within digital technologies are located. The Department has a staff of approximately 175 employees including 21 full professors (some part time) and 19 associate professors (some part time), 12 tenure track assistant professors, ~30 postdocs and ~70 PhD students, as well as 18 Tech and Admin Staff members. The student population is approximately 800. The Department’s ranking on CSRankings.org in the set of topics covered by the mentioned research groups is in top 30 in the World and top 5 in Europe. Read more about the Department of Computer Science on www.cs.au.dk

The benefits of working in Denmark

Denmark as a country offers the opportunity to pursue a career without compromising your family life and in general work-life balance in Denmark is among the best in Europe. In addition, Denmark is a safe place to live with a very low crime rate and is in general secure and equal. Denmark is considered in the top of the happiest countries in the world in international surveys. The Danish society builds on a welfare system which means your relatively high taxes goes into welfare services such as free healthcare and education. International academic staff members can usually also benefit from a special reduced tax scheme in the first years of employment. • to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. jobs.description:
The Department of Forensic Medicine at Faculty of Health Sciences at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in the field of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology as per 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a permanent full time position.

The department is part of the Faculty of Health at Aarhus University with a permanent staff of seventy employees who work in two departments delivering impartial and evidence-based public sector consultancy for the danish police. The Section of Forensic Chemistry identifies and determines the purity of drugs in both biological material and illicit drugs seized by the police. The Section of Forensic Pathology and clinical forensic medicine performs forensic autopsies, crime scene investigations and clinical forensic examinations. Both departments hold either ISO 17025 or ISO 17020 quality standard accreditations. In addition to the two sections, the department has three research units which focus on bioanalytical chemistry, forensic imaging and clinical forensic medicine. The employees work in an interface between public sector consultancy and basic and applied research, and the department has particular focus on the good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for high quality in the performance of tasks at all levels. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As Associate Professor of Molecular Bone Histology and Forensic Anthropology, you will contribute to the department’s research, teaching environment and commissioned work, and to the university’s overall strategy. You will contribute to the development of the department both individually and in collaboration with others via your research of high international quality. You will furthermore contribute to the development of the department’s commissioned work within your area of expertise. You possess professional collaborative skills and a broad academic network across disciplines and institutions, which you are able to bring into play in your contribution to the academic development of Aarhus University and its profile both locally, nationally and internationally.

• Commissioned work within the field of Forensic Anthropology

You have established yourself as a prominent researcher within molecular bone histology and you possess documented solid research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. jobs.occupation: Rethinking Converter Synchronization: 2-Year Postdoctoral Position in Battery Energy Storage Systems
jobs.description:
Are you eager to contribute to a bold experimental research project at the forefront of power electronics and energy storage? We are offering an exciting 2-year postdoctoral position for a talented researcher to investigate advanced converter synchronization and control methods for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with particular emphasis on exploiting naturally occurring acoustic and vibration information. The project combines converter control, sensing, signal processing, and experimental validation to explore new approaches toward simpler, more robust, and scalable BESS operation. This position is expected to start from 1st of January 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

About the project
The position is affiliated with the VILLUM Experiment project A-choir and the EMI/EMC In Power Electronics research group at AAU Energy. The project investigates new synchronization concepts for multi-converter BESSs by combining power electronics, sensing, signal processing, and control. A particular focus is placed on whether physical signatures naturally generated during converter operation can provide useful information for synchronization and coordination. 

You will join a research environment working across power electronics, EMI/EMC, converter control, multi-physics analysis, and experimental validation with applications including battery energy storage systems and other converter-dominated energy systems, with opportunities for collaboration across disciplines. The position also offers opportunities for international scientific exchange, participation in leading conferences, and may include research visits to relevant academic or industrial partners.

Your work tasks
You will:

• Develop and investigate synchronization and coordination methods for power electronic converters.
• Develop sensing and signal-processing methods for acoustic and vibration measurements.
• Establish and evaluate relationships between physical signatures and converter switching/operating behaviors.
• Implement and validate the developed methods using real-time control platforms, HIL, and experimental converter setups.
• Assess the proposed approaches under representative BESS operating conditions, including robustness to interference and multi-converter interactions.
• Contribute to the coordination of related research activities, and disseminate results through scientific publications, conferences, and project deliverables.
The position may also include a limited amount of teaching and supervision in areas related to your expertise.

Your competencies
We expect you to have:

• A PhD in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience in power electronics, power converter modelling and control, converter synchronization, signal processing, EMI/EMC, or related areas.
• Strong programming and experimental skills using DSP, MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, hardware-in-the-loop implementation or comparable tools.
• Experience with one or more relevant methods, such as synchronization and coordination control, digital signal processing, time-frequency analysis, data-driven modelling, or machine learning.
• Good knowledge of battery storage systems or multi-converter systems; experience with synchronization control, hierarchical control, hardware design, or AI-assisted signal would be an advantage.
• A strong scientific publication record appropriate to your career stage.
• The ability to conduct independent research, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate effectively with academic and industrial partners.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
You are not expected to be an expert in all technical areas covering power electronics, acoustic/vibration sensing, signal processing, or machine learning. Strong competence in power converter control and synchronization, together with solid experimental skills and the ability to work across sensing, EMI/EMC, and system-level interactions, is particularly important. We value scientific independence, critical thinking, strong experimental skills, and a rigorous approach to modelling, implementation, validation, and documentation.

Who we are
The position will be based in the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems” at Department of Energy in Aalborg University (AAU Energy). AAU Energy is an international research department at Aalborg University dedicated to developing clean and sustainable energy systems across electrical, thermal, and mechatronic energy technologies. We offer an interdisciplinary research environment, advanced laboratory facilities, and extensive collaboration with industry and academic partners. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg; this position is based at the Aalborg campus. Read more at www.energy.aau.dk

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

**About the Role

**As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

**

What you'll do

**Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

**

Tooling & standards**

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

**

Technical leadership & mentorship**

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

**We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.
